notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its regular and special meetings, January to December 1971, from the four quarterly volumes the San Francisco Public Library contributed to the Internet Archive (16-19minutesofsanfran1971sa). Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index, counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false (checked against the scan of 16minutesofsanfran1971sa n10). Every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the minutes state stood on or occupied the property; dated past facts the minutes state about a building; and landmark designations. A proposal on its own is not a finding. A Board of Supervisors or committee action the minutes report without its own date is framed 'by' the date of the meeting that reported it. The minutes name applicants, owners, attorneys, objectors, commissioners and staff throughout; the reader spec barred all of them from every field, and kept companies, institutions, named buildings, architects and long-dead historical figures a landmark report associates with a building.

coverage.remaining: Every page of the four 1971 volumes (16minutesofsanfran1971sa, 17minutesofsanfran1971sa, 18minutesofsanfran1971sa, 19minutesofsanfran1971sa) was read. Volumes 20-39 (1972-1980) and 40-58 (1994-2005) remain. Of the 169 unresolved, 128 are located only by a block, a corner, a bearing or a building name with no page to carry them (the City's surplus-lot sales, the transit and port acquisitions, whole-block cases); 19 have no EAS record at the number; 11 are condominium parcels today (1150 Lombard, 1598 Bay, 1400 Mission, 840 Powell, 3321 22nd Street), waiting on #446; 9 are ranges now split across parcels. The single-lot block-and-lot records were looked up in sf-parcels and EAS: those with one active lot and one address on a page or place were placed (Seward and Head-and-Brotherhood mini-parks, Laguna Honda, 507 Capp, the Presidio car barn); the rest name several lots, a retired lot, or a vacant lot with nothing to publish.
coverage.note: 1,086 OCR pages with text out of 1,704 scanned leaves, read by ten parallel readers from one written spec; 39 meetings dated, 323 findings: 162 statements of what stood on a property, 113 decisions, 38 dated past facts, 10 landmark designations. Every quote was re-anchored mechanically against its own page before the file was written (323 of 323 anchored). 154 resolved: 108 by the EAS join on a printed number (3500 Army Street by the alias ARMY=CESAR CHAVEZ), 46 by hand — named buildings the site already carries (the Hallidie Building, the Cable Car Barn, the Fire Chief's Home, Cameron House, the Metropolitan Life, Tishman-Cahill and Standard Oil towers, St. Luke's, Pacific Medical Center, the South San Francisco Opera House), the record's own block and lot, and the 266-268 Eighth Avenue range. 142 published on 71 pages (34 of them seeded, 2 Recreation and Park place pages); 12 declined: 6 already on the page from another source or an earlier volume, 4 adding nothing the page lacks, 1 a repeat within the batch, 1 published as a stated conflict in the page's unknowns instead (the Southern Pacific Building's 1917 against the page's 1916).
